Overview

Asunción as a Business Centre

Asunción is Paraguay's capital and largest city. The 2022 census counted about 462,000 residents in the city itself, a figure that has fallen as households move to neighbouring municipalities in the Central Department such as Luque, San Lorenzo and Capiatá. The wider Gran Asunción agglomeration is estimated at about 2.1 million people. The city concentrates the national government and courts, the Banco Central del Paraguay, the headquarters of most banks, finance companies and insurers, and the Bolsa de Valores de Asunción. Paraguay's agricultural exports are grown largely in the east and the Chaco, but the money behind them is often financed, contracted and litigated in Asunción.

Organisations commission investigative work connected to Asunción because it is where Paraguayan capital is raised and decisions are made. The local bond market has grown quickly: the stock exchange recorded its highest-ever trading volume in 2025, about 8.06 billion dollars, with more than 1.26 billion dollars of new issues. Investors and lenders need to understand the issuers, family groups and cooperatives behind that paper. National ministries and state companies award contracts from the capital, so procurement integrity questions also lead there. And foreign companies entering Paraguay through distributors, joint ventures or acquisitions usually deal with Asunción-based owners and advisers whose backgrounds need checking.

Typical Matters

Investigative Work Connected to Asunción

01

Bond issuer and family group diligence

Paraguay's bond market is dominated by local companies, finance houses and cooperatives, many controlled by families with interests across sectors. Before investing or lending we research issuers' owners, related companies, litigation and regulatory history and media coverage, so clients understand the group behind the paper and its connected exposures.

02

Public procurement and state contracting

Ministries, state companies and the binational energy entities make contracting decisions in Asunción. We review published procurement records, awards and protests, along with corporate links between bidders, intermediaries and officials, to support integrity reviews, bid challenges and internal inquiries by contractors and lenders.

03

Market entry and partner vetting

Foreign companies entering Paraguay often appoint distributors, agents or joint venture partners headquartered in Asunción. We confirm who owns and runs the counterparty, review disputes, tax and regulatory matters, politically exposed connections and reputation, and highlight issues for counsel to address in contracts.

04

Real estate and construction counterparties

Office towers and residential projects in Asunción's newer business districts have attracted local and foreign capital. We research developers, contractors and investors, including source-of-funds questions and links to entities named in money laundering or smuggling reporting, before clients buy, lend or partner.

05

Litigation and award enforcement support

Commercial litigation and arbitration involving Paraguayan parties usually runs through Asunción. We help counsel identify the assets, companies and affiliates of a debtor, review its prior disputes, and document the background of parties and witnesses ahead of proceedings or enforcement.

Local Context

Courts, Records and Institutions in Asunción

Courts in the capital

The Corte Suprema de Justicia sits in Asunción, as do the civil and commercial courts of first instance and appeal for the Capital judicial district, where most large commercial cases involving Paraguayan companies are heard. Proceedings are in Spanish and much of the record is now managed electronically. Counsel selects the forum, and we tailor research to its procedural rules and to what court records are available to parties and the public.

Arbitration and mediation

Institutional arbitration in Paraguay is centred in Asunción, where a centre attached to the national chamber of commerce administers commercial arbitration and mediation under the national arbitration and mediation law. Contracts with Paraguayan counterparties often refer disputes there or to international institutions. Counsel confirms the applicable rules, and we support them with factual research on parties, assets and relevant history.

Central bank and securities market

The Banco Central del Paraguay is headquartered in Asunción and supervises banks and finance companies and, through its regulations, the infrastructure of the securities market; in 2022 it authorised the stock exchange to settle trades through its real-time payment system. The Bolsa de Valores de Asunción, founded in 1977 by the national chamber of commerce, lists bonds, shares and fund units, and its public issuer filings are a useful source on Paraguayan companies.

Registries and records

The public registries of persons, companies and real estate administered under the judiciary have their principal offices in Asunción, as do the Abogacía del Tesoro's beneficial ownership registers, which are not open to public search. City property and municipal licensing records are held by the Municipalidad de Asunción, while properties in the surrounding Central Department municipalities are handled through their own municipal offices and the national cadastre.

Engagement Standard

How TDSC Scopes Matters in Asunción

TDSC has no office in Asunción and works on matters there from Nashville. We first agree with the client and its counsel the decision at stake, whether an investment in a local issuer, a contract with a state body, a new partner, a property transaction or a dispute. We then map the people, companies and assets involved and work from lawful sources: stock exchange filings, published procurement records, court information, public registry extracts obtained through Paraguayan counsel, sanctions and adverse-media screening, and Spanish-language press. Where in-person enquiries are needed we coordinate qualified Paraguayan professionals. Reports state sources and confidence, and we do not access restricted government or banking records.

TDSC has no office in Asunción. Engagements are directed from Nashville, Tennessee; where work on the ground is needed, it is performed by appropriately licensed local professionals under a written scope.

Questions

Asunción: Frequently Asked Questions

Why does so much Paraguayan due diligence lead to Asunción?

The capital concentrates the government, the central bank, the stock exchange, most bank and corporate headquarters, and the courts that hear major commercial cases. Even when farms, factories or border businesses operate elsewhere in Paraguay, their owners, financing, contracts and disputes are frequently based in Asunción, so counterparty research usually starts there.

How large is Asunción?

The 2022 census counted about 462,000 people in the city, according to INE figures reported in the press, and the city has been losing residents to the Central Department. The wider Gran Asunción agglomeration is estimated at about 2.1 million. When population matters to a client's analysis, we cite the source and definition we use.

Can you research companies that issue bonds in Asunción?

Yes. Issuers on the Bolsa de Valores de Asunción publish prospectuses and periodic information, which we combine with registry extracts, court information, media and sanctions screening. With 155 active issuers at the end of 2025, many from the same family groups, mapping related parties and cross-guarantees is often the most useful part of the review.

Can you review a Paraguayan public tender?

We review published procurement information on calls, bidders, awards and challenges, together with corporate and media records, to show links between bidders, intermediaries and officials. We do not access restricted government systems or contact evaluators. The work supports counsel in bid protests, compliance reviews and investigations involving Paraguayan public contracts.

Does TDSC have staff in Asunción?

No. TDSC has no office, staff or address in Paraguay. Engagements are scoped and managed from Nashville. Where local registry searches, interviews or site visits are needed, we coordinate qualified Paraguayan professionals and work alongside the client's Paraguayan counsel, who advise on law and procedure.
